title: Two Miles Down: The Strange World That Lives Without Sunlight
title_zh: 两英里之下：不见阳光的奇异世界
intro_zh: 本文约 960 词，介绍深海生物如何在极端的黑暗、低温与高压下生存，并配有 4 道 CET-4 阅读理解题。

paragraphs.en: Think of the ocean and most people picture sunshine, waves and white sand. Yet sunlight reaches only the top 200 metres of the sea. Below that line lies a dark, cold kingdom that covers about two-thirds of our planet's surface, and scientists believe that more than 80 per cent of it has never been seen by human eyes. This is the deep sea — the largest habitat on Earth, and still the least understood. Its conditions are extreme even by ocean standards: water close to freezing, almost no light anywhere, and a weight of water that grows heavier with every metre you sink.
paragraphs.zh: 一提到海洋，多数人想到的是阳光、海浪和洁白的沙滩。然而，阳光只能到达海面以下约200米。在这条界线之下，是一个黑暗而寒冷的王国，占地球表面的三分之二，而科学家认为其中超过80%的部分从未被人类看到过。这就是深海——地球上最大的栖息地，也是最不为人知的一处。即便以海洋的标准衡量，那里的条件也极端：水温接近冰点，到处几乎一片漆黑，而每下潜一米，水压都会无情地增加。

paragraphs.en: The deep is far from empty. Trawling in places such as Monterey Bay, biologists have caught hundreds of fish in a single afternoon, most of them silver-grey with huge eyes. There are also squid, jellyfish and worms so transparent, like wet glass, that they are noticed only by the faint shadow of their small organs. What stands out most, though, is the light. According to scientists at the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute, around three quarters of the animals caught in open water can produce light of their own. They do not use it to keep warm, and they rarely use it to find their way. Instead, the light is a language: a blue flash here, an answer a few metres away. The signal may warn a hungry neighbour to stay back, invite a mate closer, or simply say: I am still here.
paragraphs.zh: 深海远非空旷。在蒙特雷湾等海域进行拖网调查时，生物学家曾在一个下午捕获数百条鱼，它们大多是银灰色、长着巨大的眼睛。此外还有鱿鱼、水母和蠕虫，它们像湿玻璃一样透明，只有靠它们微小器官投下的淡淡阴影才能被发现。最引人注目的却是那里的光。据蒙特雷湾水族馆研究所的科学家估计，在开阔水域捕获的动物中，约四分之三能自己发光。它们并不用光取暖，也很少用光辨认方向。相反，这些光是一种语言：一道蓝色的闪光，几米外便有另一道回应。这个信号也许是在警告某个饥饿的家伙退后，也许是在邀请配偶靠近，或者只是在说：我还在这里。

paragraphs.en: Other lights are traps set by a predator. In the shallower deep, a fish called the anglerfish uses a long fin as a fishing rod, dangling it in front of a mouth full of needle teeth. The tip of the fin carries a glowing ball, and small hungry animals swim over to take a look. A female anglerfish can grow a metre long, with teeth that slope inward so that her prey has almost no chance of escape. The male stays tiny, has no lure and shows no interest in elegance. He bites the female's body and never lets go; in time the two share flesh, and even share meals. In the deep, where a single dinner may be weeks away, nothing is wasted.
paragraphs.zh: 另一些光则是捕食者设下的陷阱。在较浅的深海区，一种叫鮟鱇鱼的鱼把长长的背鳍当作钓竿，垂在长满利齿的嘴前。鳍的末端挂着一个发光的小球，饥饿的小动物便游过来一探究竟。雌鱼能长到一米长，长着向内倾斜的尖牙，让猎物几乎没有逃脱的机会。雄鱼则一直很小，没有诱饵，也谈不上优雅。它咬住雌鱼的身体，再也不松口；日子一久，两者血肉相连，连食物都共享。在深海区，一顿饭可能要等上好几个星期，浪费任何东西都不划算。

paragraphs.en: Pressure is the next problem. At sea level, about one kilogram of air rests on every square centimetre of your body. Every ten metres you sink adds roughly another atmosphere of weight. At the bottom of the Mariana Trench, some 10,900 metres down, the force is close to one tonne per square centimetre. Life is there anyway. In 2023 a Japanese team filmed a fish — a small, pale snailfish — swimming at 8,336 metres in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench in the western Pacific. Its body is jelly-like, and it has no swim bladder, nor does it need one, because at such depth a pocket of gas would tear the fish apart. Such a fish can survive because its molecules and cell membranes are shaped to resist the pressure of the water above.
paragraphs.zh: 压力则是另一重难题。在海平面，你身上每平方厘米大约承受一公斤空气的重量。每下沉10米，这个重量就增加约一个大气压。在马里亚纳海沟底部，水深约10,900米，压力接近每平方厘米一吨。尽管如此，生命依然存在。2023年，一个日本团队在西太平洋伊豆-小笠原海沟8,336米深处拍到一条鱼——一条娇小的浅色狮子鱼——正在游动。它身体呈胶状，没有鱼鳔，也不需要鱼鳔，因为在这种深度，一个气泡会把鱼撕碎。这种鱼能存活下来，是因为它的分子和细胞膜结构被塑造得能抵抗上方水体的压力。

paragraphs.en: In some places the water itself turns hostile. In 1977, scientists found hot springs on the Pacific floor near the Galapagos Islands, where water pours out at temperatures of about 400°C. At normal pressure such water would boil long before that, but two thousand metres down the huge weight of the sea locks it in liquid form. Around the vents, however, animals crowd together. Tube worms — bodies more than two metres long — reach out from them, with no mouth and no stomach. Bacteria inside their bodies can adapt to the heat and live on chemicals such as hydrogen sulphide instead of sunlight. The whole food web is built on chemistry, not on photosynthesis.
paragraphs.zh: 在某些地方，水本身也变得充满敌意。1977年，科学家在加拉帕戈斯群岛附近的太平洋海底发现了热液喷口，涌出的水温度高达约400°C。在常压下，这样的水早就该沸腾了，但在两千多米深处，海水的巨大重量把它锁在液态。然而喷口四周却挤满了动物。管虫——身体可长达两米以上——从里面伸出来，没有嘴，也没有胃。它们体内的细菌能适应高温，并以硫化氢等化学物质为生，而不是靠阳光。整个食物网建立在化学之上，而不是光合作用之上。

paragraphs.en: Near the vents there are other odd creatures: giant isopods that look like cockroaches with too many legs, bright white crabs hurrying over the rocks, and ghostly blind shrimp with a sensitive patch on their backs that can sense a vent even when its smoke hides the sun. Out in the open water, far above the bottom, some animals grow to a surprising size. The eye of the colossal squid is about 27 centimetres across — wider than a dinner plate — the largest eye recorded in the animal kingdom. In 2020 a team filmed a spiral-shaped siphonophore off the coast of Western Australia whose outer ring stretched more than 40 metres, drifting like a loosened spool of thread. Around hydrothermal vents alone, researchers say, thousands of species may still have no name.
paragraphs.zh: 喷口附近还有别的怪东西：长得像多脚蟑螂的巨型等足虫，在岩石上匆匆爬过的亮白色螃蟹，以及背上带有一块敏感光斑的幽灵般的盲虾——即使喷口的烟柱遮住了阳光，它们也能感知到。在远离海底的开阔水域里，还生活着一些体型惊人的生物。大王乌贼的眼睛直径约27厘米——比餐盘还大——这是有记录以来动物界最大的眼睛。2020年，一个团队在西澳大利亚海岸附近拍摄到一种螺旋状的管水母，它的外圈长度超过40米，漂在水里就像一卷松开的线轴。研究人员说，仅热液喷口周围，就可能还有数千个物种尚未被命名。

paragraphs.en: Why does this variety matter? Because deep-sea research keeps rewarding us. Compounds taken from deep sponges, corals and bacteria are now being tested in laboratories, and one day they may become medicines and industrial enzymes. At the same time, studying the deep forces us to face facts we would rather avoid: pieces of plastic have been found at the bottom of the Mariana Trench and under the ice of the Arctic. The deep sea is not another planet. It is right on our doorstep, in a room we have hardly entered.
paragraphs.zh: 这种多样性为什么重要？因为深海研究一直在回报我们。如今，取自深海海绵、珊瑚和细菌的化合物正在实验室里接受测试，也许有一天会变成药物和工业用酶。与此同时，研究深海也逼着我们面对一些不愿面对的事实：塑料碎片已经在马里亚纳海沟底部和北极冰层下被发现。深海不是另一个星球。它就在我们家门口，是一个我们几乎还没走进去的房间。

paragraphs.en: Since an estimated 80 per cent of the ocean has never been explored, it is no surprise that almost every dive brings back something that puzzles scientists. The Ocean Census programme, launched in 2023, hopes to describe 100,000 new species by 2030. That is a large aim, but the deep is large enough to hold it. After all, we have mapped the surface of Mars in greater detail than our own sea floor — and the strangest landscape on Earth may lie just a few miles below the water, quietly waiting.
paragraphs.zh: 既然估计仍有80%的海洋从未被探索过，几乎每次下潜都带回让科学家困惑的东西也就不足为奇了。2023年启动的“海洋普查”计划希望在2030年前描述10万个新物种。这个目标很大，但深海的体量足以容纳它。毕竟，我们对火星表面的测绘，比对自己海底的测绘还要细致——而地球上最陌生的风景，或许就横卧在几英里深的水面之下，静静等候。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The strange creatures of the deep sea and how they live in extreme conditions.
The pollution of the oceans and ways to protect sea animals.
The race between countries to own the resources of the ocean floor.
Why people fear the deep sea more than they fear high mountains.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文从黑暗、发光、捕食、高压、热液喷口等角度介绍深海生物及其极端生存方式，A 最全面。B 只涉及末段一句，C、D 文中未提。

questions.q: According to the passage, what is true of the anglerfish?
options: The female is blind in the dark and hunts by sound.
The male is much bigger than the female and hunts alone.
The male is very small and attaches himself to the female for life.
Both the male and the female use glowing teeth to attract food.
questions.explain: 细节题。第三段说雄鱼一直很小，会咬住雌鱼身体再也不松口，甚至共享血肉和食物，故 C 正确。文中说雌鱼把发光小球作诱饵，不是牙齿发光，A、D 与原文不符，B 与原文相反。

questions.q: Why does the snailfish found at 8,336 metres have no swim bladder?
options: Because food is so scarce there that it is no longer needed.
Because at such depth a pocket of gas would destroy the fish.
Because its large eyes have taken over the job of the bladder.
Because scientists removed the bladder before filming it.
questions.explain: 细节题。第四段明确说在这种深度一个气泡会把鱼撕碎，所以它不需要鱼鳔，B 正确。A、C、D 文中均无依据。

questions.q: The word 'rewarding' in Paragraph 7 is closest in meaning to:
options: paying money to someone for help
passing something from parent to child
questions.explain: 词义题。rewarding 在此与“给钱、加重、传给下一代”无关，而是“带来有用成果或好处”之意，由后文药物与工业酶的例证可验证，故选 B。
